title: Insurer Remittances, Short Pays and Closing of Insurance Claim Repairs Repair Orders
content:
**Remittances.** Insurer remittances reduce the insurer balance of an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order and are recorded under the insurer's own payment reference, verbatim.

**Short pays.** When a remittance leaves the insurer balance above zero (a short pay), the shortfall stays owed while the center supplies the insurer the documentation it asks for. A shortfall is written off as a short-pay write-off only when it is no more than the short-pay write-off figure of the insurer's active Insurer Program Agreements agreement, and never by moving it to the customer; a larger shortfall stays owed.

**Closing.** A repair order closes once it has been delivered (or, for a total loss, once the vehicle has been released to the insurer) and both balances are zero: both the customer balance and the insurer balance on the repair order are zero. Both balances are read from the repair order's own money history in the system before it is closed.

**Corrections.** Billing corrections in either direction name the entry they correct.

## Short-pay outcomes (hypothetical agreement write-off figure USD 25.00)

| Shortfall after the remittance | Outcome |
|---|---|
| USD 25.00 | may be written off as a short-pay write-off (no more than the figure) |
| USD 25.01 | stays owed by the insurer |
| any amount | never moved to the customer |

## Closing table

| Delivered, or total-loss vehicle released to the insurer | Customer balance | Insurer balance | Closes |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | zero | zero | yes |
| yes | zero | above zero | no |
| yes | above zero | zero | no |
| no | zero | zero | no |
